```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 3.9, fig.align = "center", out.width = "90%"
)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

wildlife <- read_rds("data/wildlife_clean.rds")

model_data <- wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(height), !is.na(speed)) %>%
  mutate(height_1000 = height / 1000, speed_10 = speed / 10)

m_height <- glm(damaged ~ height_1000, data = model_data, family = "binomial")
m_both <- glm(damaged ~ height_1000 + speed_10, data = model_data, family = "binomial")

or_height_alone <- tidy(m_height, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term == "height_1000")
or_both <- tidy(m_both, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
or_h <- or_both %>% filter(term == "height_1000")
or_s <- or_both %>% filter(term == "speed_10")
```

## The data

- Source: FAA Wildlife Strike Database, shared through TidyTuesday (July 2019)
- Strikes reported by pilots, airlines, and airports, mostly voluntary
- Only the 4 biggest US airlines (American, Delta, Southwest, United), 1990-2018
- One row = one reported strike
- 56,978 strikes, 19 variables after dropping 2 ID columns
- Key variables: damage level, height and speed at impact, phase of flight, time of day, species

Why this dataset: I am interested in aviation safety, and bird strikes are one of the most common risks to aircraft.

## Initial questions

- When a plane hits a bird, what decides whether the plane gets damaged?
- Does it matter how high the plane is?
- Does it matter which phase of flight it is in (take-off, climb, approach, ...)?

My guess going in: strikes higher up are worse, because planes are flying faster and birds up there may be bigger.

## Data preparation

- Removed `r 56978 - nrow(wildlife)` strikes with no damage information, leaving `r format(nrow(wildlife), big.mark = ",")`
- Damaged = Yes if damage was minor, uncertain, or substantial; No if none
- Phase of flight had inconsistent labels ("APPROACH", "Approach", "approach"), so I fixed the capitalization and kept the 5 main phases
- Grouped height into 5 bins for plots
- Bird size from labels like "Unknown bird - small"
- Height is missing for `r round(100 * mean(is.na(wildlife$height)))`% and speed for `r round(100 * mean(is.na(wildlife$speed)))`% of strikes, so the model only uses strikes with both (`r format(nrow(model_data), big.mark = ",")`)

## Damage is rare: about `r round(100 * mean(wildlife$damaged == "Yes"), 1)`% of strikes

```{r phase-plot}
wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(phase)) %>%
  group_by(phase) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(damaged == "Yes")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = phase, y = rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Climb and descent have the highest damage rates",
    x = "Phase of flight", y = "Strikes with damage"
  )
```

## Higher strikes look worse...

```{r height-plot}
wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(height_bin)) %>%
  group_by(height_bin) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(damaged == "Yes")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = height_bin, y = rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Damage rate by height at impact",
    x = "Height at impact", y = "Strikes with damage"
  )
```

## ...but height and speed go together

```{r phase-table}
wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(phase), !is.na(height), !is.na(speed)) %>%
  group_by(phase) %>%
  summarise(
    `Height (ft)` = median(height),
    `Speed (kts)` = median(speed),
    Damaged = scales::percent(mean(damaged == "Yes"), accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  rename(Phase = phase) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

\vspace{0.4cm}

Planes that are higher up are also flying faster. So the height pattern could really be a speed effect.

Refined question: Is a strike more dangerous because the plane is high, or because it is fast?

## Main analysis: logistic regression

Response: damaged (Yes/No). Height per 1,000 ft, speed per 10 knots.

```{r model-table}
bind_rows(
  or_height_alone %>% mutate(model = "Height only"),
  or_both %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>% mutate(model = "Height + speed")
) %>%
  mutate(
    term = recode(term, height_1000 = "Height", speed_10 = "Speed"),
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    `95% CI` = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", conf.low), "-", sprintf("%.2f", conf.high)),
    `p-value` = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.2f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  select(Model = model, Term = term, `Odds ratio`, `95% CI`, `p-value`) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

\vspace{0.3cm}

- Once speed is in the model, height no longer matters (odds ratio `r round(or_h$estimate, 2)`)
- Each extra 10 knots multiplies the odds of damage by about `r round(or_s$estimate, 2)`

## Predicted chance of damage

```{r predict-plot}
expand_grid(speed_10 = seq(10, 30, by = 1), height_1000 = c(0, 1, 5)) %>%
  augment(m_both, newdata = ., type.predict = "response") %>%
  mutate(height = factor(paste(height_1000 * 1000, "ft"), levels = c("0 ft", "1000 ft", "5000 ft"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = speed_10 * 10, y = .fitted, color = height)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "At the same speed, height barely changes the risk",
    x = "Speed at impact (knots)", y = "Predicted chance of damage",
    color = "Height"
  )
```

## Bird size matters a lot

```{r size-plot}
wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(bird_size)) %>%
  group_by(bird_size) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(damaged == "Yes")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bird_size, y = rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Large birds cause damage far more often",
    subtitle = "Strikes recorded as unknown small, medium, or large bird",
    x = "Bird size", y = "Strikes with damage"
  )
```

## Limitations: reporting changed over time

```{r year-plot, fig.height = 3}
wildlife %>%
  group_by(incident_year) %>%
  summarise(reports = n(), rate = mean(damaged == "Yes")) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(reports, rate), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(measure = if_else(measure == "reports", "Number of reports", "Share with damage")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = incident_year, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL)
```

- More reports but a lower damage rate: probably more minor strikes were reported later, not safer planes
- About half the strikes are missing height or speed
- Results are associations, not causes

## Conclusion

- About `r round(100 * mean(wildlife$damaged == "Yes"), 1)`% of reported strikes damaged the aircraft
- Strikes higher up look more damaging, but that is mostly because planes up there are faster
- After accounting for speed, height does not matter; speed does
- Bird size is the other big factor: large birds cause damage about `r wildlife %>% filter(!is.na(bird_size)) %>% group_by(bird_size) %>% summarise(rate = mean(damaged == "Yes")) %>% summarise(round(max(rate) / min(rate))) %>% pull()` times as often as small birds

Next step: add bird size to the model, using strikes where the bird size was recorded.
